topic_relevance.B02: direct: GSIP relaxed-disjunction separation, two exact lower-level algorithm counterexamples, and strict boundary failure.

definitions.name: GSIP and its relaxed SIP
definitions.statement: GSIP requires g(x,y)≥0 for every y satisfying h_j(x,y)≤0. With hbar=max_j h_j, exact disjunction is [g≥0]∨[hbar>0]. Its relaxation uses hbar≥0, equivalently max{g,hbar}≥0 for all y. The relaxed separation problem is inf_y max{g(x,y),hbar(x,y)}, not min g subject to hbar≤0.

definitions.name: Assumption1 and global lower master
definitions.statement: Compact X,Y; continuous f,g,hbar; f*=fL is separately assumed. For a given ε>0 either infeasible or an ε-optimal xs with a common δ>0 and [g(xs,y)≥δ]∨[hbar(xs,y)≥δ] for every y. A finite master uses the relaxed disjunction and is solved globally.

theorem_cards.label: Counterexample1: exact GSIP LLP does not separate the relaxed SIP
assumptions: Empty initial index set; exact global GSIP LLP min_y g subject hbar≤0; always choose its minimizer y_k=x_k at the positive master iterates.
theorem_cards.statement: GSIP feasible set [−1,−1/2) has unattained infimum1/2; relaxed SIP feasible set [−1,−1/2] has minimum1/2. Nevertheless x_k=y_k=2^{1−k}, selected g<0 and hbar<0 every iteration, and lower bounds approach0 rather than1/2.
proof_steps: 作者反例：g≤4−10<0 throughout the product. The GSIP is feasible exactly when its lower-index set is empty, x<−1/2; replacing >0 by ≥0 adds the boundary.
作者反例：each finite relaxed cut simplifies to −2x+y_k≥0, hence x_{k+1}=x_k/2.
作者定位原证明错误：hbar(x_k,y_k)<0 for each k does not imply one K with hbar(x_ℓ,y_k)<0 for all ℓ>k≥K. Here hbar(x_ℓ,y_k)=−2·2^{1−ℓ}+2^{1−k}>0 once ℓ>k+1.
本次核验：for every ε>0 choose η=min(ε/2,1/4), xs=−1/2−η and δ=2η; f(xs)≤f*+ε and hbar(xs,y)≥δ for all y. Thus the example meets the stated Slater assumption, not merely compactness.
gaps: The infinite infimum/attainment difference is a genuine strict-boundary issue; f*=fL is not automatic for general GSIP.

theorem_cards.label: Counterexample2: solving AUX LLP at every iteration still fails
assumptions: X=Y=[−1,1], f=−x, g=−y−10, hbar=min{−2x+y,−x}; continuous but hbar is a function in its own right, equivalently one scalar lower constraint.
Empty initial index set; GSIP LLP solved globally; AUX minimizes hbar over y∈Y with g(x_k,y)≤α g(x_k,y_k); α=0.95.
Generated index sets contain the AUX minimizers.
theorem_cards.statement: GSIP has feasible set [−1,−1/2), relaxed SIP [−1,−1/2], and common infimum1/2. First master x1=1, GSIP LLP y1=1 with value−11, AUX domain[0.45,1] and minimizer0.45. Its cut yields x2=0. Every later AUX optimizer lies in[0.45,1] and adds no tighter cut; all subsequent masters remain0 and lower bounds stay0.
proof_steps: 作者反例：g<0 everywhere, so relaxed cuts require min{−2x+y,−x}≥0, equivalently x≤0 and x≤y/2.
作者反例：at x1=1, AUX objective min{−2+y,−1} is minimized at y=0.45. At x=0 its objective is zero on all allowed y∈[0.45,1]; any such index keeps the master feasible set[−1,0].
本次核验：the true relaxed separation at x=0 chooses y=−1 and has max{g,hbar}=−1<0; it is excluded by AUX since g(0,−1)=−9>−10.45. Thus the missing cut is not a numerical/local-optimality artifact.
本次核验：xs=−1/2−η with η=min(ε/2,1/4) gives hbar(xs,y)≥min(2η,1/2+η)>0 for all y and f(xs)≤1/2+ε, so all stated assumptions hold.
gaps: Different α or initial cuts may change this one instance; they do not restore a universal theorem for the quoted algorithm.
This note suggests using the correct SIP LLP and references later approaches; it does not itself supply a general convergence theorem for those external GSIP solvers.

constant_dependence.explicit: Counterexample2 fixes α=0.95, AUX lower endpoint11α−10=0.45, first post-cut master0, gap1/2. Slater witness uses η=min(ε/2,1/4) and positive δ=min(2η,1/2+η).
constant_dependence.dependence: No convergent GSIP iteration rate is proved. Strict-feasibility margin is not a uniform future-iterate margin.

endpoint_limits: Boundary hbar=0 distinguishes exact GSIP from the closed disjunction.
The scalar hbar=min{−2x+y,−x} in CEx2 is allowed as one continuous constraint; it need not be the maximum of those two displayed linear expressions.
Generic equality f*=fL cited from external [3] is not a universal claim.
reusable_methods: Derive the actual relaxed SIP oracle from its full disjunction before importing an exchange proof.
Audit diagonal strict inequalities separately from quantified cross-iterate inequalities.
Test lower-level filters for exclusion of a still-violating index, including hbar boundary points.
unchecked: All local pages and references read; external algorithms and generic-feasible-closure result are not independently certified.
These counterexamples reject the cited lower-bound claims, not all GSIP exchange methods or upper-bounding components.
No finite tolerance rate, general solver implementation or center-cube transfer asserted.
